_about: Public-domain John Newland Maffitt (1794-1850), Irish-born Methodist revivalist and chaplain of the US House of Representatives, for the Word Hoard: Tears of Contrition, Pulpit Sketches, Literary and Religious Sketches, and his sermons A Plea for Africa and A Voice from the Ocean. Texts are from Internet Archive scans. Added 2026-10-24 by lane A, round 135 (my pick); Adam may veto the whole shelf. Every printing dated before 1930, so public domain in the US. No uids minted.

maffitt-pulpit-sketches: Pulpit sketches, sermons, and devotional fragments (Boston, 1828)
maffitt-plea-africa: A plea for Africa. A sermon delivered at Bennet Street Church, in behalf of the American Colonization Society, July 4, 1830 (Boston: E. W. Crittenden, 1830)
maffitt-literary-religious: Literary and religious sketches (New York, Press of T. Harries, 1832)
maffitt-voice-ocean: A voice from the ocean: sermon, delivered in the House of representatives, Sunday, July 31, 1842, to the memory of Rev. George G. Cookman (Washington, Printed by P. Force, 1842)

_excluded.maffitt-secular: the Oratorical Dictionary, Ireland: a Poem and The Carrier Dove are not theology
_excluded.maffitt-others: the trial report and the 1906 Life are about him; Nautilus and the Embury memorial are by other Maffitts
